faq.title: Scientific Methodology & Agronomic FAQ (Field Parameterized)
faq.q1: How does Terrashift+ calculate crop suitability without an AI black box?
faq.a1: Terrashift+ pairs physical agronomy with calibrated machine learning surrogates. On this sampled field, the engine balances {rain} rainfall against {et0} FAO-56 Penman-Monteith evapotranspiration, evaluating crop root zones using Saxton-Rawls pedotransfer hydrology (AWC: {awc}) and RUSLE slope physics ({slope} slope). Calibrated quantile gradient boosting models then establish 80% confidence bands without unverified hallucination.
faq.q2: How do the 3 Statistical & SI methodologies compare on my field?
faq.a2: 1) Statistical Distribution (SPI/SPEI) tracks multi-year climatic anomalies and SMAP root-zone Z-scores ({gwet_z}σ). 2) Physically-Based Modeling (FAO-56 & RUSLE) simulates daily soil moisture depletion and water stress index (WSI). 3) Calibrated ML Surrogate (GMM & Quantile Boosting) identifies your field regime as '{cluster}' with a Mahalanobis distance of {mahalanobis}, ensuring predictions remain strictly in-distribution.
faq.q3: Why does the system flag a [DATA GAP] instead of inventing numbers?
faq.a3: In operational agronomy, feeding synthetic approximations to a farmer risks real-world crop failure. If a satellite cannot resolve a pixel (e.g. cloud cover on optical MODIS, coastal masks on SoilGrids, or temporary API downtime), Terrashift+ explicitly flags the gap and invites farmer in-situ calibration rather than manufacturing deceptive fallbacks.
faq.q4: What is the purpose of Stage 02 Ground-Truth Calibration?
faq.a4: Satellite and model data have coarse native resolutions (NASA POWER: ~50km, ISRIC SoilGrids: 250m). Microclimates, tree canopy shading, and past organic soil amendments can create discrepancies. The ground-truth inputs allow farmers and agronomists to anchor the model to actual physical soil reports and local rain gauge records.
faq.q5: Which NASA missions and open datasets are ingested live?
faq.a5: Terrashift+ ingests NASA POWER v2.0 (GMAO MERRA-2 daily agroclimatology), NASA EOS Terra MODIS (MOD13Q1 250m NDVI via ORNL DAAC), NASA Earthdata CMR (SMAP L4, ECOSTRESS, GPM IMERG, GEDI L4A Biomass, GRACE-FO), NASA GIBS WMTS (MODIS True Color, SMAP Surface Soil Moisture, Land Surface Temperature), ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0, and Open-Meteo DEM 90m.

about.title: About TerraShift+
about.subtitle: Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data — Dar es Salaam & Nairobi Regional Collaboration
about.mission_desc: TerraShift+ was developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 to empower smallholder and commercial farmers in East Africa and globally with physics-informed, climate-resilient crop rotation planning. By fusing multi-mission NASA Earth observations with deterministic agronomic models (FAO-56 Penman-Monteith, Saxton-Rawls pedotransfer, RUSLE soil erosion) and farmer ground-truth overrides, the system identifies high-confidence rotation sequences that disruption pest cycles, preserve root-zone moisture, reduce soil loss, and stabilize agricultural livelihoods without replacing local agronomic expertise.

about.data_stack_desc: Ingesting 8 multi-mission Earth observation and partner data streams: NASA POWER v2.0 (solar, precipitation, ET0), SMAP L4 (9km root-zone soil wetness), GPM IMERG v07B (precipitation calibration), MODIS MOD13Q1 / Terra-Aqua (250m 16-day NDVI vegetation canopy), ECOSTRESS (70m Land Surface Temperature thermal stress), GEDI / SRTM (topography and slope), and iSDAsoil v2 30m / ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 (soil texture, pH, organic carbon).
about.methodology_desc: Couples FAO-56 dual crop coefficient water-stress indexing with quantile gradient boosted regression (P10/P50/P90 margin distributions), Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR10 worst-decile safety floor), and Saxton-Rawls available water capacity (AWC).
about.disclosure_desc: In compliance with NASA Space Apps guidelines, AI models (Gemini LLMOps, Quantile Gradient Boosting) serve strictly as assistive synthesizers bounded by deterministic physical equations and domain guardrails. All agronomic calculations are grounded in published FAO and USDA physical models.
